newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LOWERY, LICKLITER SHARE FIRST-ROUND DISNEY LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LOWERY, LICKLITER SHARE FIRST-ROUND DISNEY LEAD.

text.p: Steve Lowery and Frank Lickliter shared the first round lead at the Walt Disney World Classic with rounds of nine under par 63 Thursday.
Jeff Sluman and Joey Gullion were a stroke behind at 64.
Lowery had an eagle, eight birdies and a bogey in his round at the Palm, considered the most difficult of the three courses, none of which are considered very difficult for professionals.
Only 11 players in the 132-man field were over par, with Davis Love's four over 76 at the Palm the highest score shot.

The tournament, played in a pro-am format, uses three of the Disney resort courses, the host Magnolia course, where Lickliter played on Thursday; the Palm, where Lowery shot his 63; and the Lake Buena Vista course, where Sluman and Gullion played.
The professionals, playing with three amateurs, rotate between the courses during the first three rounds, with Sunday's conclusion pros only at Magnolia.
The last full-field event of the 1996 PGA Tour season, the Disney is a tournament of last chances for most of its participants.
Lickliter is currently 138th on the money list, just over $30,000 behind 125th place, and needs a good finish to keep his exempt status in 1997.

Sluman, the 1988 PGA Champion, isn't concerned about being exempt for the tour, but needs to stay in the top 30 money winners to be exempt for next year's Masters and U.S. Open, as well as next week's $3 million Tour Championship.
Lowery is in 79th place, with no wories about the top 125, and no chance at the top 30.

"It's an advantage, probably," said Lowery. "I'm very fortunate not to be scrambling for the top 125. I've got nothing on my mind this week but playing golf. For a lot of the other guys, this is a big week."
For Gullion, who has to finish third or better to keep his card, it is a big week.

"There's a lot of pressure. No one wants to go back to (qualifying) school. Playing in a pro-am may make it easier though. My amateurs kept me loose, and thinking about them keeps your mind off of your own situation."
